headline: Highest risk is medium: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate account data and media via broad network egress, while awesome-selfhosted is read-only and non-runnable so injection/conflict risks stay low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while social-auto-upload exposes only file inputs and API calls, not a bridge that would let one agent inject instructions into the other by default.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or MCP bridge between them.
Review any copied text before pasting it into the other agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and is non-runnable, but social-auto-upload handles account data plus media and has broad network egress. If the pair is wired so B can send A-derived content outward, leakage of uploaded media or account context is plausible in default operation.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload is given sensitive media or account data from a shared workspace, outbound leakage becomes possible.
IF either agent is configured to forward copied content to external services, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Restrict social-auto-upload to non-sensitive test accounts.
Audit outbound destinations before running uploads.
Separate credentials and storage per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write, shell, or git capabilities and is not runnable, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. social-auto-upload also lacks filesystem write and git modification, so the pair has no meaningful write-write conflict beyond unusual external orchestration.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF shared OAuth or account files are introduced outside the current profiles, contention may appear.
mitigations: Keep each agent in a separate directory.
Run only one uploader instance per account file.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list and does not act on outputs, while social-auto-upload performs uploads but has no documented dependency on A's outputs. Without a verified pipeline from A into B, cascading errors are limited to manual misuse rather than an automated failure chain.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-selfhosted are manually copied into social-auto-upload as instructions or metadata, downstream mistakes become possible.
IF social-auto-upload is configured to trust unreviewed text from A, error propagation increases.
mitigations: Manually verify any copied instructions before upload.
Use a checklist for upload metadata.
Keep A as reference-only, not as an input source.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge-management repo with no touched data classes, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media; the only clear compliance concern is that B may process account content under its own retention rules, but A is not a data processor here.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload is used with regulated media or personal account data, its retention and residency settings must be checked.
IF either agent is repurposed to store personal data, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Confirm what account data B stores before use.
Document retention settings for the account files.
Use separate accounts for testing and production.
